skill.name: prisma-database-setup
skill.description: Configures Prisma ORM for PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB, SQL Server, CockroachDB, and Prisma Postgres, including clients, adapters, environment variables, and troubleshooting.
skill.summary: Set up Prisma schemas, connections, adapters, and generated clients for supported databases.
skill.author: prisma

security_audit.summary: The skill contains documentation and examples for Prisma configuration. The flagged paths, environment variables, credentials, and backticks are fixed examples with no prompt injection, secret exfiltration, or executable audit payload.

content.value_statement: Prisma setup varies by database provider and major version. This skill provides provider-specific schemas, connection guidance, adapters, client generation, and troubleshooting steps.
actual_capabilities: Configures Prisma schemas for PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB, SQL Server, CockroachDB, and Prisma Postgres.
Explains Prisma 7 SQL configuration through prisma.config.ts and database-specific driver adapters.
Keeps MongoDB projects on the supported Prisma 6 workflow.
Shows environment variable and connection string formats using placeholder values.
Guides Prisma Client installation, generation, imports, and single-instance reuse.
Troubleshoots provider-specific connection, schema, ID, and compatibility issues.
limitations: Provides guidance but does not verify that your database server is available.
Uses placeholder credentials that must be replaced with secure values.
Does not cover production migration planning, backups, or disaster recovery.
MongoDB guidance targets Prisma 6 because the documented Prisma 7 SQL workflow does not apply.

use_cases.title: Start a SQL project
use_cases.description: Configure a new Prisma project with the correct provider, adapter, connection variables, and generated client.

use_cases.title: Build with local SQLite
use_cases.description: Create a lightweight local database setup and understand SQLite paths, adapters, and feature limits.

use_cases.title: Standardize database configuration
use_cases.description: Compare provider requirements before changing databases or deploying Prisma across runtime environments.

prompt_templates.title: Initialize Prisma
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure Prisma for {database} in my {runtime} project. Show required packages, schema settings, environment variables, client generation, and a basic client instance.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new project

prompt_templates.title: Add the correct adapter
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Prisma {database} setup for {runtime}. Identify the required driver adapter, packages, generated client import, and connection settings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Configure Prisma Client for an existing schema

prompt_templates.title: Switch database providers
prompt_templates.prompt: Move this Prisma project from {current_database} to {target_database}. Review the schema and configuration, then list required changes and compatibility concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose deployment connections
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this Prisma connection issue for {database} on {runtime}: {error_message}. Check URL format, adapter choice, pooling, environment values, and provider settings.

output_examples.input: Set up Prisma 7 with PostgreSQL in a Node.js project.
output: Install Prisma Client, Prisma CLI, the PostgreSQL adapter, and the pg driver.
Configure the PostgreSQL provider and datasource environment variable.
Generate the client and create one reusable adapter-backed client instance.

output_examples.input: Configure Prisma for an existing MongoDB application.
output: Keep the project on the latest supported Prisma 6 release.
Use the MongoDB provider and the classic Prisma Client generator.
Confirm replica-set support and ObjectID mappings before synchronizing the schema.

output_examples.input: My Prisma MySQL application reports too many connections.
output: Reuse one Prisma Client instance for each application process.
Review the MySQL connection limit and adapter pool settings.
Set an appropriate connection limit for the deployment environment.

best_practices: Keep real database credentials outside source control and use separate values for each environment.
Confirm the Prisma major version and database provider before applying adapter guidance.
Regenerate Prisma Client after every schema change and reuse one client instance per process.
anti_patterns: Do not copy SQL driver adapter instructions into a MongoDB project.
Do not commit environment files or real connection strings.
Do not run production migrations without backups, review, and an approved deployment plan.

faq.question: Which databases are covered?
faq.answer: The guides cover PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, MongoDB, SQL Server, CockroachDB, and Prisma Postgres.

faq.question: Does this skill support MongoDB?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses the Prisma 6 MongoDB workflow because the Prisma 7 SQL adapter workflow does not apply.

faq.question: Does this skill create a database?
faq.answer: Most guides expect an existing database. The Prisma Postgres guide also documents its authenticated provisioning command.

faq.question: Does this skill store my credentials?
faq.answer: No. Examples use placeholders and named environment variables, while your project controls the real values.

faq.question: Can I use Bun?
faq.answer: Yes. Run Prisma CLI commands through the documented Bun invocation so Prisma uses the Bun runtime.

faq.question: Does this skill manage production migrations?
faq.answer: No. It covers provider and client setup, but production migration planning, backups, and recovery remain your responsibility.
